summary: This notice announces a program for Value Chain Based Commercial Banana and Fruit Farming Promotion. It invites individual farmers, groups, and cooperatives to apply for support in cultivating bananas and various fruits commercially.
details: This notice was published by Agriculture Knowledge Center, Bara. Applicants should read the attached PDF and complete the process before: Closed !!!.
eligibility: Individual farmers, farmer groups, or farmer cooperatives.
For individuals: Must own or lease a minimum of 10 Ropani of land for banana cultivation or 25 Ropani for fruit cultivation.
For groups/cooperatives: Must own or lease a minimum of 25 Ropani of land for banana cultivation or 50 Ropani for fruit cultivation.
Land must be suitable for banana/fruit farming, accessible by road, and have irrigation facilities.
Access to markets for the agricultural produce.
Applicants must demonstrate technical and managerial capacity.
Applicants must have financial capacity, including own investment.
Preference will be given to applicants who have already established a nursery or have prior experience in related fields.
required_documents: Copy of Nepali citizenship certificate (for individual applicants).
Registration certificate and renewal certificate (for groups and cooperatives).
Minutes of the decision to participate in the program (for groups and cooperatives).
Copy of Tax Registration Certificate (PAN/VAT).
Land ownership certificate or land lease agreement (if land is rented).
Map of the proposed project area.
For existing businesses: Business registration certificate (for limited companies registered for at least 10 years, or for firms/companies/groups/cooperatives registered for at least 1 year).
For new businesses: A detailed project proposal.
Technical report/project report.
Bank account statement.
Clear statement regarding the distribution of benefits among members (for groups and cooperatives).
Recommendation letter from the local government (Ward office) verifying the applicant's status as a professional farmer or registered group/cooperative.
Details of the proposed investment cost.
Details of the proposed quantity of production.
Project's Internal Rate of Return (IRR) / Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) analysis.
Details of the project's financial sustainability and viability.
benefits: The notice describes a 'promotion program' for commercial banana and fruit farming. Specific financial benefits like subsidies or grants are not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but the program aims to provide support and opportunities for commercial agricultural development.
application_process: Application forms can be obtained from the Project Implementation Unit, Bara, or downloaded from http://bara.akc.gov.np.
Applications can be submitted online or in person.
The cost of the application form is non-refundable.
contact_information: Organization: Project Implementation Unit, Bara, Agriculture Development Directorate, Department of Agriculture, Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development, Government of Nepal.
important_points: The Project Implementation Unit reserves the right to accept or reject any application without providing a reason.
Submission of false documents will result in legal action against the applicant.
Project selection will be based on criteria including technical evaluation and prioritization.
Applicants must include a social and environmental impact assessment in their proposal.
Applicants must commit to following all program guidelines and rules.
plain_explanation: This notice from the Nepal government is for farmers interested in starting or expanding commercial banana and fruit farming. The program aims to support these ventures, especially those that focus on the entire value chain (from farm to market). To apply, you need to be an individual farmer, a farmers' group, or a cooperative, and you must have a significant amount of suitable land (at least 10 Ropani for individuals for banana, more for fruit farming or groups). You'll need to gather many documents, including your citizenship, land ownership papers, business registration (if applicable), a detailed project plan, and financial records. The government unit in Bara will review applications based on your technical ability, financial capacity, and project viability. However, applications for this program are currently closed.
